title: Dispatch: 21 picture annotations and none AGREED; seats agree on what is drawn (kind 90%) but not on how they word it (features 35%): close the vocabulary before annotating more
statement: The route to evidence for language now runs through the drawings (text statistics are reproduced by a one-table reuse chain, P-G-007, P-G-009). State: 21 blind picture annotations of six folios are on the record (V-001..V-021) and none is AGREED; the best is f70v2 at 0.747, and f66r, f72r3 and f99r are DISAGREE. Measured over every pair of seats on the same folio, using the scorer's own pairing (vs/registry.py picture_agreement): kind agrees on 537 of 596 paired objects (0.90); shared feature values agree on 688 of 1977 (0.35); on average only 0.29 of the feature keys two seats used are in common; and of label line ids used by either seat, 212 of 535 are used by both. So seats see the same objects and largely disagree on wording, which no amount of re-annotation fixes. Next, in order: (1) a code: change adding a closed feature vocabulary to picture.json (per kind, a short list of keys with enumerated values; free text kept in a notes field that agreement ignores) and pairing objects by position (ring and angle, or reading order) rather than list order; (2) re-annotate the folios with it (the PIC-<folio> steps); (3) only then run the picture-text statistics (branch code-P-L4-013-fleet-opus adds them to vs/dsl.py; they refuse until AGREED objects exist). Label assignment on zodiac rings stays a blind-annotation limit: ids carry no position, so labels should be joined by a position map made by a non-annotator.
